title: Speculative Hook Methods (Template Method Creep)
pattern: Defining empty or default-returning hook methods in traits or abstract structures solely for hypothetical future extensibility.
why_bad: Pollutes the API contract, forcing implementers to look at unused hooks, complicating execution tracking, and adding zero active value.
detection: Trait methods with empty default bodies (`{}`) that are never overridden by any of the trait's active implementers.
counterexample: Public plugin architectures or frameworks where third-party consumers are expected to override specific hooks.
fix: Delete the hook method and simplify the trait pipeline.
source: Erich Gamma et al., *Design Patterns* (1994), Template Method; Joshua Kerievsky, *Refactoring to Patterns* (2004), Chapter 8.
